title: Regeneration of LeTID degradation in p‐PERC photovoltaic modules using DC bias
content:
Abstract

This study systematically investigates the regeneration of light- and elevated-temperature-induced degradation (LeTID) in p-type PERC photovoltaic mini-modules using DC bias under dark conditions. LeTID degradation was induced under 1 sun illumination at 85°C, followed by regeneration using forward and reverse DC bias in the dark. Under forward bias (I = 0.454 A, V = 2.8 V) for 13 h, the short-circuit current density (J sc) recovered from 88.72% to 96.0%, while the open-circuit voltage (V oc) recovered to approximately 100.0% of its initial value. The efficiency (η) and maximum power (P mpp) also showed substantial recovery. Under reverse bias (V = V oc) for 15 h, J sc recovered from 88.98% to 94.7%, with corresponding improvements in the other photovoltaic parameters. The results indicate that forward-bias regeneration is primarily driven by excess carrier injection, whereas reverse-bias recovery suggests the involvement of electric-field-assisted mechanisms. Overall, this work demonstrates module-level regeneration and provides a comparative analysis of forward and reverse DC bias as practical recovery pathways for LeTID-affected p-PERC modules.
